switch_rule: Every entry names the ONE config key that switches its module ON and OFF, as {table, key, on, off}. 'table' is one of the four config tables (rails.config_tables.CONFIG_TABLE_NAMES: judges, knowledge_views, observe, toolkits); 'key' is a dotted path that starts with that table and names one of its entry keys, with '<phase>' as the placeholder for a program's phase because a module's admission is about the module and not about one program's phase names; 'off' is the table's null arm, which composes to the same config hash as the table being absent (core.config.drop_null_arms), which is what makes the OFF arm a twin of the pre-table baseline rather than a third cell identity. 'proof' names the test that composes both arms and asserts they differ in exactly that one key. A FIFTH class, 'run', covers a module that is one config key and has no table entry because it is per-run and the four tables are per-phase: 'key' is the FLAT config key the fragment carries, it must be on the closed allowlist rails.config_tables.RUN_LEVEL_SWITCH_KEYS, 'off' is the key absent or the driver's documented default, and the entry owes a 'falsifier' -- kind 'request-bytes-identical' plus the receipt that proved it -- whose MANIFEST.sha256 the check re-verifies. That falsifier is the whole licence for being outside the tables: a module that moves one byte of the request cannot produce one and belongs in a table.

switch.what_flew: The sealed arm DID fly through this key: configs/baseline/e21-buf90-zero-locked-scored4-prefetch1.json is the comparator's own baseline fragment plus obs_prefetch_depth 1, and the proof test diffs those two committed fragments.
switch.why_this_class: obs_prefetch_depth is read flat by core.driver.run and reproduction.obs_loop and decides how many samples of lookahead the driver keeps in flight. It is per-RUN, while observe, knowledge_views, judges and toolkits are per-PHASE and each of them changes the request the frozen core sees. This one provably changes no request byte, which is both why it has no table entry and why it is allowed to have none.
